A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the case of a young infant, the conjunctivae are the best place for the inspection of petechial hemorrhage.

in the infantile cases, the degree of petechial hemorrhage in conjunctivae and the degree of histological findings in the lung and pancreata, are very different from those in adult cases, and that these differences can be used for the evaluation of the cause of infantile asphycia.
in infantile asphixia, the conjunctivae hemorrhages are not reliable in diagnosis, but the histological and immunhistochemical examination of the lungs and pancreas is useful.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the histology findings of the lung, the pancreas, and the conjunctivae hemorrhage of infantile asphixia cases should be carefully examined, in order to avoid misdiagnosing infantile asphyxial cases.
the histological findings in the lungs and pancreas are very useful for the evaluation of the cause of sudden death of infants.
we should not misdiagnose genuine accidental suffocation or homicidal suffocation cases as SIDS cases.
